beats.label: S1 · The 100 land
beats.text: The Ark drops 100 juvenile prisoners to test if Earth is survivable, led by Clarke and the reckless Bellamy, who convinces them to ditch their vitals wristbands.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the two leaders and severs the Ark's ability to know the ground is habitable.

beats.label: S1 · Grounders exist
beats.text: The kids discover Earth is not empty: hostile Grounders spear Jasper, and Clarke's group learns they are surrounded by clans who see them as invaders.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces the enemy that defines every season going forward.

beats.label: S1 · Ark culls its own
beats.text: Believing the 100 are dead, the Ark seals off Section 17 and kills 300 people to save air; the kids fire flares just after, proving the ground is alive.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The culling drives Abby's push to reach the ground and fractures the Ark's leadership.

beats.label: S1 · Finn's massacre averted
beats.text: Clarke negotiates a fragile peace with Grounder commander Anya's people, but a spooked Jasper opens fire and the meeting collapses into war.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes that the Sky People's mistakes, not malice, keep escalating the war.

beats.label: S1 · Clarke and Bellamy lead
beats.text: After a viral attack and mutual near-deaths, Clarke and Bellamy become co-leaders of the 100, with Raven, Octavia and Lincoln in orbit around them.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Locks in the show's central duo and the Octavia/Lincoln bridge to the Grounders.

beats.label: S1 · Dropship inferno
beats.text: Cornered by a full Grounder assault, Jasper ignites the dropship rockets and incinerates 300 attackers, apparently killing Finn and Bellamy in the blast.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets up the moment the survivors are taken by an unknown third party.

beats.label: S1 · Mount Weather
beats.text: The dazed survivors are gassed and abducted; Clarke wakes in a spotless white quarantine room and sees Monty locked across the hall in Mount Weather.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The cliffhanger and the antagonist of Season 2.

cliffhanger.text: Clarke and the surviving kids are prisoners inside the pristine Mount Weather facility. The Ark is falling apart above them, with Jaha choosing to bring the whole station down to Earth.
questions: Who are the people running Mount Weather, and why did they take the 100?
Did Finn and Bellamy actually die in the dropship blast?
Can the Ark's remaining population survive re-entry to the ground?

characters.name: Clarke Griffin
characters.line: Doctor's daughter turned reluctant leader of the 100; wakes up locked inside Mount Weather.

characters.name: Bellamy Blake
characters.line: Ruthless co-leader of the camp who came down to protect his sister; last seen fighting off Grounders at the dropship.

characters.name: Octavia Blake
characters.line: Bellamy's illegal-born sister, now bonded to the Grounder Lincoln and fleeing with him.

characters.name: Raven Reyes
characters.line: Zero-g mechanic who launched herself down to find Finn; the group's engineer and Finn's ex.

characters.name: Finn Collins
characters.line: Peacemaker of the 100 who slept with Clarke before Raven arrived; presumed dead in the dropship blast.

characters.name: Lincoln
characters.line: The Grounder who saved Octavia and defied his people to help the Sky Kids.

characters.name: Abby Griffin
characters.line: Clarke's mother and Ark chief medical officer, now on the ground with the surviving adults.

characters.name: Marcus Kane
characters.line: Former hardline councilman who has begun questioning his own severity; on the ground with Abby.

characters.name: Thelonious Jaha
characters.line: Chancellor who stayed behind on the dying Ark to buy the others time.

characters.name: Jasper Jordan
characters.line: The kid speared in the pilot; ignited the dropship rockets and was taken with the others.

characters.name: Monty Green
characters.line: The 100's tech; imprisoned in Mount Weather across the hall from Clarke.

beats.label: S2 · Mount Weather's price
beats.text: Clarke discovers Mount Weather's residents cannot survive outside and are harvesting captured Grounders' blood to treat their own radiation sickness.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Defines the moral trap Clarke will spring by season's end.

beats.label: S2 · Sky People and Grounders
beats.text: The Ark survivors regroup as Camp Jaha and eventually meet the Commander of the twelve clans, Lexa, who agrees to a truce against the mountain.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces Lexa, the political axis of the rest of the season and beyond.

beats.label: S2 · Clarke kills Finn
beats.text: To stop Lexa executing Finn for massacring a Grounder village, Clarke stabs him herself in a mercy killing, sealing the alliance in his blood.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Removes Finn permanently and cements the Clarke–Lexa bond.

beats.label: S2 · Lexa's love, Lexa's betrayal
beats.text: Lexa kisses Clarke and confesses her feelings, then at Mount Weather's door abandons the alliance to save only her own captured people.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The betrayal that shapes Clarke's mistrust and isolation next season.

beats.label: S2 · Irradiating the mountain
beats.text: Abandoned by the Grounders, Clarke and Bellamy pull the lever together and irradiate all of Mount Weather, killing every man, woman and child inside.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The atrocity that drives Clarke's Season 3 exile and her name Wanheda.

beats.label: S2 · Jaha finds A.L.I.E.
beats.text: Chasing rumours of a City of Light across the desert, Jaha reaches a lush mansion and meets A.L.I.E., an AI in the form of a woman in red.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Plants the antagonist and mythology of Season 3.

cliffhanger.text: Mount Weather is a graveyard and Clarke has walked away from her people, unable to face what she did. Jaha has found an AI who thanks him for delivering her a nuclear warhead.
questions: Where will Clarke go now that she cannot bear to stay?
What does A.L.I.E. actually want with the survivors of humanity?
Can the fragile Grounder-Sky People alliance survive Lexa's betrayal and Mount Weather's fall?

characters.name: Clarke Griffin
characters.line: Wracked with guilt after committing genocide to save her friends; walks off alone into the woods.

characters.name: Bellamy Blake
characters.line: Went undercover inside Mount Weather and helped Clarke pull the lever; now the de facto leader in her absence.

characters.name: Lexa
characters.line: Commander of the twelve clans; betrayed Clarke by cutting a separate deal for the Grounder captives.

characters.name: Abby Griffin
characters.line: Chancellor of the Sky People; barely rescued from Mount Weather's bone marrow harvest.

characters.name: Marcus Kane
characters.line: Reformed councilman now working alongside Abby and Lexa's people toward peace.

characters.name: Octavia Blake
characters.line: Trained by Grounder warrior Indra as her second; increasingly Grounder in loyalty.

characters.name: Lincoln
characters.line: Recovered from being turned into a Reaper; now stuck under a Grounder death sentence at Camp Jaha.

characters.name: Raven Reyes
characters.line: Left with a permanent leg injury after Abby's field surgery; the group's engineer.

characters.name: Jasper Jordan
characters.line: Traumatised by watching his Mountain Weather love Maya die when Clarke irradiated the level.

characters.name: Monty Green
characters.line: The tech who hacked Mount Weather's air system for Clarke; now bearing his own share of the guilt.

characters.name: Thelonious Jaha
characters.line: Ex-chancellor turned prophet, now inside A.L.I.E.'s mansion and evangelising the City of Light.

characters.name: John Murphy
characters.line: Made it to A.L.I.E.'s island with Jaha; watched a video of the previous occupant kill herself over the launch codes.

beats.label: S3 · Wanheda hunted
beats.text: Clarke has been living alone as Wanheda, the Commander of Death, when Ice Nation prince Roan captures her for the bounty and delivers her to Lexa in Polis.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Reintroduces Clarke and sets up Polis as the season's political stage.

beats.label: S3 · A.L.I.E.'s City of Light
beats.text: Jaha spreads A.L.I.E.'s pill through Arkadia, promising freedom from pain; Raven takes one to escape her chronic injury and begins losing memories of Finn.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The mechanic of the season's true antagonist.

beats.label: S3 · Lexa dies, Flame revealed
beats.text: Clarke and Lexa finally sleep together; minutes later Titus shoots Lexa by accident, and Clarke learns the Commander's spirit is an AI chip in her neck.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Kills Lexa, seeds the Flame mythology, and shatters the Grounder–Sky alliance.

beats.label: S3 · Pike's coup and massacre
beats.text: Farm Station's Pike is elected Chancellor and, backed by a guilt-ridden Bellamy, massacres the Grounder army sent to protect them; Lincoln is later executed.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Snaps Octavia from Bellamy and Skaikru; Lincoln's death is the wound she carries forward.

beats.label: S3 · Origin of the Flame
beats.text: Flashbacks reveal A.L.I.E. caused the original nuclear apocalypse, and her creator Becca fled to Earth carrying the second, better AI that became the Commander's Flame.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Unifies the Grounder religion with the show's sci-fi backbone.

beats.label: S3 · Kill switch
beats.text: With Ontari brain-dead and Clarke made Nightblood via transfusion, Clarke takes the Flame, enters the City of Light, and pulls A.L.I.E.'s kill switch — freeing everyone.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Resolves A.L.I.E. and forces the pivot to the coming radiation crisis.

beats.label: S3 · Praimfaya warning
beats.text: A.L.I.E.'s last confession: the world's decaying nuclear reactors are melting down and Earth has roughly six months before it burns again.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The direct set-up for Season 4's entire plot.

cliffhanger.text: A.L.I.E. is dead and the world is free of the chip. In the same breath, Clarke has learned that the surface is about to become uninhabitable and only she knows.
questions: How do a few hundred people survive an apocalypse in six months?
With Pike dead and Lexa gone, who leads the Grounder clans now?
What does Clarke do with a truth that will terrify everyone she tells?

characters.name: Clarke Griffin
characters.line: Carrying the Flame's knowledge and A.L.I.E.'s warning; the only person who knows the ground is dying.

characters.name: Bellamy Blake
characters.line: Working to earn back Clarke's trust after backing Pike's massacre of the Grounder army.

characters.name: Octavia Blake
characters.line: Killed Pike herself in revenge for Lincoln; alienated from Bellamy and Skaikru.

characters.name: Raven Reyes
characters.line: Freed from A.L.I.E.'s chip with residual AI knowledge lodged in her brain.

characters.name: Abby Griffin
characters.line: Recovering from being one of A.L.I.E.'s puppets, back working as Skaikru's doctor.

characters.name: Marcus Kane
characters.line: Political leader of Skaikru again after Pike's fall.

characters.name: Roan
characters.line: King of the Ice Nation and one of the few Grounder leaders still functional.

characters.name: Indra
characters.line: Trikru warrior chief; Octavia's former mentor, still allied with Kane.

characters.name: John Murphy
characters.line: Escaped Polis after posing as Flamekeeper for the impostor Commander Ontari.

characters.name: Thelonious Jaha
characters.line: Freed from A.L.I.E. but responsible for spreading her chip; his standing is destroyed.

characters.name: Jasper Jordan
characters.line: Sober, hollowed out and openly nihilistic after Maya's death.

characters.name: Monty Green
characters.line: Killed his own mother to save Octavia; quieter and heavier for it.

beats.label: S4 · Race the death wave
beats.text: Clarke's group confirms A.L.I.E.'s warning: nuclear plants are melting down and a global death wave will scorch Earth in months.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The clock that structures the season.

beats.label: S4 · Nightblood is the answer
beats.text: Luna's Grounder blood proves immune to radiation, so Abby and Raven race to engineer synthetic Nightblood to save everyone.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets up the medical stakes and the eventual failure of the plan.

beats.label: S4 · Arkadia burns
beats.text: Ilian, driven mad by A.L.I.E.'s legacy, torches Arkadia, destroying Skaikru's fallback shelter and their plan to ride out Praimfaya inside it.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Forces the shift to the Second Dawn bunker as the only refuge.

beats.label: S4 · One bunker, twelve clans
beats.text: Jaha finds a Second Dawn bunker under Polis that can hold only 1200 people; a conclave to the death is held to decide which clan takes it.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets up Octavia's ascension and the bunker's political structure.

beats.label: S4 · Blodreina rises
beats.text: Octavia enters the conclave and wins, then decrees the bunker will be shared equally by all twelve clans, taking her seat as their queen.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes Octavia's authority for the six-year jump.

beats.label: S4 · Two arks, no earth
beats.text: As Praimfaya arrives, Clarke stays behind to power the sat dish and Bellamy's group launches to the Ark; Clarke's Nightblood lets her survive the wave alone.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The physical separation that defines Season 5.

beats.label: S4 · Six years later
beats.text: Clarke has raised a young Nightblood girl, Madi, in the last green valley; a prison ship from before the apocalypse suddenly lands beside them.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces Madi and the Eligius arrivals — the whole engine of Season 5.

cliffhanger.text: The world has burned and healed. Clarke and Madi are alive in the only fertile valley left, watched over by a strange spacecraft that has just descended from orbit.
questions: Who are these people from a ship built before the apocalypse?
Are Bellamy's crew on the Ark and Octavia's people in the bunker still alive?
How much of Clarke will Madi have when the others return?

characters.name: Clarke Griffin
characters.line: Nightblood; sole surface survivor of Praimfaya, mother-figure to Madi for six years.

characters.name: Madi
characters.line: The natural Nightblood child Clarke found and raised in the valley.

characters.name: Bellamy Blake
characters.line: Leader of the seven who launched to the Ark and have been there six years, believing Clarke dead.

characters.name: Octavia Blake
characters.line: Blodreina — dictator of the twelve clans locked in the Second Dawn bunker for six years.

characters.name: Raven Reyes
characters.line: The pilot who got Bellamy's crew to space; alive on the Ark.

characters.name: Abby Griffin
characters.line: In the bunker with Octavia's people, struggling with her role after Praimfaya.

characters.name: Marcus Kane
characters.line: In the bunker; Octavia's uneasy conscience and Abby's partner.

characters.name: Indra
characters.line: Bunker enforcer, kept Octavia in power alongside her daughter Gaia.

characters.name: John Murphy
characters.line: On the Ark with Bellamy's crew; paired with Emori.

characters.name: Emori
characters.line: Grounder outcast, Murphy's partner, on the Ark.

characters.name: Echo
characters.line: Former Ice Nation spy banished by Roan; on the Ark with Bellamy after fleeing Earth.

characters.name: Monty Green
characters.line: On the Ark with Harper; the group's engineer alongside Raven.

characters.name: Harper McIntyre
characters.line: On the Ark; Monty's partner.

beats.label: S5 · Eligius arrives
beats.text: The prison transport disgorges Diyoza's crew of pre-apocalypse convicts, who claim the last green valley on Earth as their own.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces Diyoza and the war over the only habitable land.

beats.label: S5 · Everyone returns
beats.text: Bellamy's group lands and reunites with Clarke and Madi; Octavia's bunker is dug out after six brutal years, and all three factions descend on the valley.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Puts every surviving human on a collision course.

beats.label: S5 · Blodreina versus the valley
beats.text: Octavia leads Wonkru — hardened by cannibalism in the dark year of the bunker — to conquer Eden, refusing any peace short of surrender.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets Octavia as the season's antagonist among her own people.

beats.label: S5 · Madi becomes Commander
beats.text: To stop Octavia, Gaia gives Madi the Flame and ascends her as the new Commander; Clarke is horrified that her child now leads a war.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes Madi's Commander status and Sheidheda's foothold in her head.

beats.label: S5 · Clarke's betrayal
beats.text: To protect Madi, Clarke sides briefly with McCreary and hands over her own people, before Madi's connection to past Commanders pulls her back.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The rupture between Clarke and everyone else going into Season 6.

beats.label: S5 · Valley destroyed
beats.text: McCreary's dying-man protocol nukes Eden; humanity flees to the Eligius mothership as Earth's last habitable ground is destroyed.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Ends Earth as a setting and forces the move to a new planet.

beats.label: S5 · A new world
beats.text: 125 years later, Clarke and Bellamy wake to Monty and Harper's son Jordan; the couple chose to skip cryosleep, living out their lives and leaving video diaries behind.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The setting change for Season 6.

cliffhanger.text: Earth is gone. The survivors are in cryosleep on the Eligius ship, headed for a distant moon Monty found, chaperoned by his son Jordan.
questions: What is waiting for them on the new world?
Can Clarke, Octavia and Bellamy ever repair what happened in the valley?
Is the Dark Commander Sheidheda actually gone from Madi's Flame?

characters.name: Clarke Griffin
characters.line: Isolated from her people after betraying them to protect Madi; heading to a new world in cryo.

characters.name: Bellamy Blake
characters.line: Reunited with Echo; the group's moral centre, wary of Clarke, in cryo.

characters.name: Madi
characters.line: The child Commander, secretly haunted by the memories of the previous Commanders including Becca Pramheda.

characters.name: Octavia Blake
characters.line: Deposed Blodreina, shunned by the people she led; her cruelty in the bunker is public knowledge.

characters.name: Raven Reyes
characters.line: Still the group's engineer; helped fight the Eligius crew from orbit.

characters.name: John Murphy
characters.line: Fully reformed by his relationship with Emori.

characters.name: Emori
characters.line: Murphy's partner; increasingly a leader in her own right.

characters.name: Echo
characters.line: In a stable relationship with Bellamy; still lethal, still Azgeda-trained.

characters.name: Charmaine Diyoza
characters.line: Former terrorist and Eligius captain; pregnant, defected from her own crew.

characters.name: Marcus Kane
characters.line: Badly wounded and put back in cryosleep in the hope of saving him later.

characters.name: Abby Griffin
characters.line: In cryo, still hooked on pills after the bunker's dark year.

characters.name: Indra
characters.line: Wonkru's warrior authority, no longer under Octavia's spell.

characters.name: Gaia
characters.line: Flamekeeper who put the Flame in Madi; carries the religion.

characters.name: Jordan Green
characters.line: Monty and Harper's grown son; the only one awake when Clarke and Bellamy come out of torpor.

beats.label: S6 · Welcome to Sanctum
beats.text: The survivors land on the moon Alpha, ruled by the Primes — the founding families of the Sanctum colony, who present themselves as benevolent hosts.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces the season's world and antagonists.

beats.label: S6 · Bodysnatchers
beats.text: The Primes' immortality is a lie: their mind drives overwrite the consciousness of Nightblood hosts, killing whoever the body used to be.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The horror underneath Sanctum's utopia.

beats.label: S6 · Josephine takes Clarke
beats.text: To buy time before another host matures, Russell and Simone wipe Clarke and install their daughter Josephine in her body.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The season's central body-horror plot and the source of Bellamy's grief.

beats.label: S6 · Clarke survives inside
beats.text: A remnant of A.L.I.E. in Clarke's head lets her hide in her own mindscape; she taps Morse to Bellamy to prove she is still alive.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Explains how Clarke comes back and what Bellamy carries next.

beats.label: S6 · The rebellion against the Primes
beats.text: With Gabriel's help Clarke ejects Josephine; posing as Josephine she reveals the Primes' harvesting to Sanctum, sparking a bloody uprising.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Ends the Primes as a ruling class.

beats.label: S6 · Sheidheda escapes the Flame
beats.text: Under threat, Raven deletes the Flame to save Madi — but the Dark Commander Sheidheda has already uploaded himself somewhere else.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Plants the Season 7 antagonist inside Sanctum.

beats.label: S6 · The anomaly opens
beats.text: The mysterious anomaly outside Sanctum surges; Diyoza's grown daughter Hope steps out, stabs Octavia at the anomaly's edge, and Octavia vanishes.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The direct cliffhanger for Season 7.

cliffhanger.text: The Primes are overthrown, but Sheidheda has escaped into some unknown host, and Octavia has just been stabbed by Diyoza's now-adult daughter Hope and pulled through the anomaly.
questions: Where — and when — has the anomaly taken Octavia?
Where has Sheidheda gone now that the Flame is destroyed?
Who is Hope, how did she grow up so fast, and who sent her?

characters.name: Clarke Griffin
characters.line: Restored to her own body; the world knows she survived being erased.

characters.name: Bellamy Blake
characters.line: Mourned Clarke, got her back; leading the group again in Sanctum.

characters.name: Madi
characters.line: Freed from Sheidheda when Raven deleted the Flame; no longer Commander.

characters.name: Octavia Blake
characters.line: Stabbed by Hope and disappeared into the anomaly; whereabouts unknown.

characters.name: Raven Reyes
characters.line: Killed the Flame to save Madi; carrying that on top of everything else.

characters.name: John Murphy
characters.line: Accepted Prime immortality and helped Josephine impersonate Clarke; only turned when Emori betrayed her and Josephine wounded him.

characters.name: Emori
characters.line: Murphy's partner; posed as Prime Kaylee during the rebellion.

characters.name: Echo
characters.line: Bellamy's partner, nearly made a host for the Primes before killing Ryker to escape.

characters.name: Abby Griffin
characters.line: Mind-wiped by Russell and killed to make her body a host for Simone Prime.

characters.name: Gabriel Santiago
characters.line: The original Prime, hiding in a young body; ally who helped extract Josephine from Clarke.

characters.name: Charmaine Diyoza
characters.line: Also lost through the anomaly earlier this season.

characters.name: Hope Diyoza
characters.line: Diyoza's now-adult daughter, who stepped out of the anomaly and stabbed Octavia.

characters.name: Russell Lightbourne
characters.line: The last surviving Prime, imprisoned by the survivors.

characters.name: Sheidheda
characters.line: The Dark Commander; uploaded himself out of the Flame before Raven deleted it.

characters.name: Jordan Green
characters.line: Monty and Harper's son; heartbroken after the Prime he loved turned out to be a body-thief.

beats.label: S7 · The Disciples take Bellamy
beats.text: Bellamy is dragged through the anomaly by invisible soldiers; Echo, Gabriel and Hope pursue him, learning the abductors are the Disciples of Bardo.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Kicks off the season's multi-planet chase.

beats.label: S7 · Time dilation
beats.text: The anomaly connects planets across a black hole, so months on one world can be years on another; Hope reveals she and Octavia grew up separated by decades.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The physics rule that governs every reunion this season.

beats.label: S7 · Sheidheda takes Russell
beats.text: Sheidheda's uploaded mind resurrects itself in the imprisoned Russell's body and begins quietly building a following in Sanctum.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Explains where the Dark Commander went and sets up his Sanctum coup.

beats.label: S7 · Cadogan's Last War
beats.text: The Disciples are the descendants of the Second Dawn cult led by Bill Cadogan, who believes a final test awaits humanity through the anomaly.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The season's true antagonist and mythology reveal.

beats.label: S7 · Bellamy converted, Bellamy killed
beats.text: Marooned on Etherea, Bellamy embraces the Disciples' faith; when he sides with Cadogan against his friends, Clarke shoots him dead.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The most consequential character death of the season.

beats.label: S7 · Sheidheda falls, Sanctum burns
beats.text: In parallel, Sheidheda seizes Wonkru, massacres Sanctumites, and is finally killed by Indra as the survivors escape to Earth and Bardo.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Closes the Sanctum plot and clears the board for the finale.

beats.label: S7 · Transcendence
beats.text: A judge appears in Abby's form to test humanity; Octavia's plea for peace passes the test and everyone but Clarke transcends into pure energy.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The series ending, framed for a viewer who has just watched it.

beats.label: S7 · Clarke's peace
beats.text: Barred from transcending because she murdered Cadogan, Clarke returns alone to a healed Earth; her friends choose to descend from transcendence to live out their lives with her.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The final resting state of every surviving character.

cliffhanger.text: Humanity is over as a species: nearly everyone has transcended into a form of light. Clarke, denied the test for killing Cadogan, is left alone on the regrown Earth — until her friends choose to come back down and live out mortal lives with her.
questions: What does 'humanity' even mean now that almost everyone has become something else?
How do the returned friends rebuild a life with each other after everything?
Can Clarke find peace on an Earth that is finally quiet?

characters.name: Clarke Griffin
characters.line: Killed Bellamy and later Cadogan; excluded from transcendence, home on a restored Earth with the friends who chose to return.

characters.name: Bellamy Blake
characters.line: Died at Clarke's hand after converting to the Disciples' faith.

characters.name: Octavia Blake
characters.line: The one who talked humanity through the final test; transcended, then chose mortality.

characters.name: Raven Reyes
characters.line: Took the test on humanity's behalf; transcended, then descended to live with the others.

characters.name: John Murphy
characters.line: Carried Emori's mind drive in his own head to keep her alive; both descended together.

characters.name: Emori
characters.line: Mortally injured when the bunker collapsed on Earth and died before reaching Sanctum; preserved in Murphy's head until they descended together.

characters.name: Echo
characters.line: Wounded in the final fight; descended with the others.

characters.name: Indra
characters.line: Killed Sheidheda; descended with the others.

characters.name: Madi
characters.line: M-Capped by Cadogan into a permanent catatonic state; transcended and did not come back.

characters.name: Gabriel Santiago
characters.line: Destroyed the Flame for good and died from Sheidheda's attack before transcendence.

characters.name: Hope Diyoza
characters.line: Charmaine's daughter, now with the survivors on Earth.

characters.name: Levitt
characters.line: The Disciple scientist who defected for Octavia; descended with them.

characters.name: Jordan Green
characters.line: Monty and Harper's son; among those who chose to return to Earth.
